Ben / Karthik —

Thanks for the context. Below is Legal's recommended compromise and the drafting approach we should propose to Sylvan. This balances Sylvan's procurement requirement for defend-and-control while protecting Redwood's financial exposure and preserving the ability to recover costs in narrow situations.

Summary of recommended position (commercial redline included):
1) Redwood will have "defend-and-control" responsibility for third-party claims alleging that the Service infringes a third party's intellectual property, provided Redwood has sole discretion to select counsel and manage the defense.
2) Redwood will not agree to unconditional settlement authority. Redwood may settle claims up to $75,000 without Customer's prior written consent. Settlements above $75,000 require mutual written consent; if mutual consent cannot be reached within 10 business days, either party may seek mediation, and Redwood's settlement liability is capped at $250,000 unless Redwood elects to pay more voluntarily.
3) Redwood may seek reimbursement for costs and damages that result from Customer's breach, misuse, or unauthorized modifications (list examples). Reimbursement for Redwood's defense costs for covered third-party IP claims is limited to amounts agreed in a post-claim cost allocation process unless there is a finding of Customer culpability.
4) Evidence handoff SLA: Customer will provide a completed evidence matrix (using the attached template) and named triage contact within 48 hours of notice of claim; failure to timely provide evidence may limit Customer's rights under the indemnity and shift higher cost responsibility to Customer.
5) Insurance / escrow: Redwood agrees to consider using insurer funds or escrow for settlements above the cap; we will provide primary evidence of insurability upon request.

Proposed redline snippet for insertion into the Order Form (send as track changes if you want to keep their doc):
"Redwood will defend and control, at its expense, any third-party claim alleging that the Service infringes a third party's intellectual property rights; provided, however, that (i) Redwood shall seek Customer's written consent for any settlement in excess of Seventy Five Thousand Dollars (US$75,000), such consent not to be unreasonably withheld; (ii) if the parties cannot reach agreement on settlement within ten (10) business days, the parties will engage in mediation; and (iii) Redwood's aggregate liability for settlements under this indemnity shall be capped at Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (US$250,000), except to the extent Redwood elects to pay amounts in excess of such cap. Customer shall promptly provide the evidence matrix and a named triage contact within forty-eight (48) hours of receiving notice of the claim; failure to do so shall relieve Redwood of obligations to the extent Redwood's ability to defend is prejudiced."

Rationale: 1) $75k settlement approval threshold gives us room to resolve routine claims without delay; 2) $250k cap limits catastrophic exposure while still providing meaningful coverage; 3) the evidence SLA protects our ability to defend efficiently and avoid unnecessary costs; 4) the insurer/escrow reference gives procurement a path to fund larger settlements without Redwood taking full balance-sheet risk.

Next steps: Ben, propose we send this redline back to Lina with the rationale and offer a short call (30 minutes) to walk through the settlement thresholds and evidence SLA. Karthik — please prepare a 2-line commercial justification (why $75k/$250k makes sense vs. other thresholds) to help procurement.

If Sylvan accepts, we should capture the evidence handoff and triage contact in the onboarding checklist and route a copy to Security & Ops.
